<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a standard nvchecker TOML configuration for the lito-bin AUR package. It configures nvchecker to monitor the GitHub repository "litocpp/lito" for new releases, using the "v" prefix for tags. The configuration is minimal and routine: it specifies the source type (GitHub), the repository name, enables use of the latest release, and sets a tag prefix. There are no network requests, obfuscated commands, dangerous eval/base64 usage, or unexpected file operations within this file itself. It simply tells the packaging tool where to check for upstream releases — a normal part of AUR package maintenance.

The file contains no code that exfiltrates data, downloads and executes external scripts, or modifies system files beyond standard packaging workflows. All elements (source, github, use_latest_release, prefix) are standard nvchecker configuration directives.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices for a prebuilt binary distribution. The package downloads official GitHub release tarballs from the project's own repository (litocpp/lito), verifies SHA256 checksums, and installs the binary via `install -Dm755` into `$pkgdir/usr/bin/`. There are no eval, base64, curl|bash, or other dangerous command patterns. The `source` array includes a README fetch from raw GitHub, which is unconventional but benign — it merely retrieves documentation. All checksums are provided with actual values (not SKIP). The package() function performs only expected file operations: installing the binary, schema files, README, and license. No network requests occur during build, no system modifications outside the package scope, and no code execution beyond the application's intended function.
</details>

</summary>
